p_intro: Serracapriola preserves a rich heritage of churches and places of worship, a living testimony of centuries of faith and popular devotion.
mercurio_storia: Dedicated to the martyr San Mercurio, a Roman soldier converted to Christianity, this is one of the oldest churches in Serracapriola. According to tradition it was built in the early medieval period, when the cult of oriental martyrs spread through southern Italy via Basilian monks. The church preserves traces of votive frescoes and a wooden statue of the Saint.
silvis_storia: The church of Santa Maria in Silvis — 'in the woods' — stands in an isolated position in an area once covered by dense forests. Of medieval, probably Lombard origin, it was a destination for seasonal pilgrimages by rural communities. The venerated image of the Madonna was invoked by farmers for the protection of crops and livestock.
cappuccini_storia: The Convent of the Capuchin Friars was founded in the 16th century during the Counter-Reformation. The Capuchins, a reformed branch of the Franciscan Order, played a fundamental role in the religious, social and charitable life of Serracapriola. After the Napoleonic suppressions of the 19th century the building changed use, but the church remained a reference point for the faithful. Among the Capuchin friars who stayed at this convent was also Saint Padre Pio of Pietrelcina, a connection that makes the place even more cherished by the popular devotion of Serracapriola.
anna_storia: The church of Sant'Anna, dedicated to the mother of the Virgin Mary, is a place of special devotion for the families of Serracapriola. Built in the Baroque period by a local confraternity, the church celebrates its feast on July 26th. The interior preserves an altar with the statue of the Saint depicted with the young Mary and Saint Joachim.
angelo_storia: Dedicated to Archangel Michael, patron of southern Italy, the church of Sant'Angelo reflects the widespread Michaelic devotion of Puglia and the Gargano. The presence of a church dedicated to the Archangel in Serracapriola is documented from at least the 16th century and is linked to the pilgrimage route to the Sanctuary of San Michele on the Gargano.
trinita_nome: Church of the Most Holy Trinity
trinita_storia: The church of the Most Holy Trinity was built by a local confraternity, as was customary in southern Italy between the 16th and 17th centuries. The building preserves a main altar with a fine painting depicting the Trinity and some period sacred furnishings.
grazie_nome: Church of Santa Maria delle Grazie
grazie_storia: The church of Santa Maria delle Grazie, built in the 17th century, is dedicated to the Madonna venerated as a dispenser of graces and miracles. It originally stood at the gates of the town to welcome travellers and devotees. The interior preserves numerous ex-votos — small painted tablets — testifying to the graces received by the faithful over the centuries.
p_nota: For information on Mass times and church opening hours contact the Parish of Serracapriola.
